newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka steps up security ahead of new year.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka steps up security ahead of new year.

text.p: Sri Lanka has stepped up security in the capital Colombo and its suburbs ahead of the Sinhala and Tamil new year that falls next weekend, police said on Monday.

They said hundreds of policemen from elsewhere in the island were being deployed to man key installations in Colombo and keep vigil in crowded markets to thwart possible attacks by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
The Sinhala and Tamil new year falls on April 13-14, and thousands of people are arriving in Colombo for pre-festival shopping.
Colombo's deputy inspector general of police, D.M.T.B. Dissanyake, said on Monday that mobile police patrols will cover city streets to minimise the risk of rebel attacks.
He told the state-owned Observer newspaper that even cadets from the police training school have been included in the security exercise.
The LTTE are fighting a 13-year-old war for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE says the number is higher.
